R1-retention.text: Events in a topic can be read as often as needed-unlike traditional messaging systems, events are not deleted after consumption.

R1-append.text: When a new event is published to a topic, it is actually appended to one of the topic's partitions.

R2-next.text: This means that the position of a consumer in each partition is just a single integer, the offset of the next message to consume.

R2-after-process.text: It can read the messages, process the messages, and finally save its position. In this case there is a possibility that the consumer process crashes after processing messages but before saving its position.

R3-write-confirm.text: The number of acknowledgments the producer requires the leader to have received before considering a request complete.

A1-committed-next.text: The committed offset should always be the offset of the next message that your application will read.

A1-after-business.text: In the example below we commit offset after we finish handling the records in each partition.

technicalBoundaries: ProducerConfig ACKS_DOC133–147: acks=all waits current ISR; no promise all configured replicas always caught up. TopicConfig219–231 additionally requires min.insync.replicas threshold. Illustrative RF3/minISR2 is a selected configuration, not universal default. Acks is not fsync or a never-loss guarantee.

KafkaConsumer72–89 distinguishes poll/read position from committed recovery position. Manual Offset Control213–289 supports processing before commit and next-message offset. Processing offset0 then committing1 is valid in a chosen contiguous example, not a claim offsets are always consecutive.

KafkaConsumer135–148 requires poll for group liveness. API408–410 pause/resume controls fetching assigned partitions in future poll calls. Pausing assigned partition does not mean stopping poll indefinitely without rebalance risk.

Introduction81: records are not deleted on consumption. Select cleanup.policy=delete and finite retention for teaching. Deletion works by retention/segments, not an exact per-record second timer; no infinite retention promise.
Introduction83 orders events within a topic-partition; no global FIFO over all partitions.

Website accepted status, stored business results and webpage querying results are teaching application design. Do not attribute business status/query API to Kafka. Commit is progress metadata, neither page notification nor atomic commit with arbitrary external business DB.
Input count minus finished-business count is original illustrative arithmetic, not measured Kafka throughput or automatically equal to logEndOffset−committedOffset.
limitations: No live Kafka cluster experiment, throughput measurement or fault injection; this is source verification of chosen mechanism statements.
